commits.edited_message:
ar: Add Windows Archive file support

Archives in ar format as written by Windows tools like lib.exe, separate
strings in string table directly with \0 instead of /\n.

GNU ar translates backslashes into slashes before the /\n check.

Handle both for improved compatibility, which also allows ar archives to
contain files in a directory structure.

Keep one spare NUL past the on-disk filename table so an empty name at
the end of a Windows table is still a C string.

Resolves #546

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

Keep the filename table buffer the same length as the on-disk table
skip consumed; member header offsets are relative to that length.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

ar: Improve error messages

Always use the term filename table and merge filename table size checks
into one.

An offset equal to the filename table length is an empty name when the
table was normalized with a trailing NUL, not a missing-name error.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The out-of-bounds read appears only when all three edits are combined; any single edit and any pair stays in-bounds. The Windows-table commit appends one spare NUL and records it in strtab_term so an empty name at offset == strtab_size would be a C string, but lookup still rejects number >= strtab_size, so that byte is never read. The skip commit then copies the table into a fresh buffer of exactly the on-disk strtab_size, because member-header offsets are relative to the length skip consumed, and it leaves strtab_term set. With the old comparison that index is still rejected; without the spare allocation the copy is the same length as the buffer it replaces. The error-message commit treats number == strtab_size as that empty name when strtab_term is set. Alone the flag is clear, so the offset is still rejected; with the spare NUL still allocated, strlen stops on a real terminator inside the buffer. Only the three together let archive_entry_copy_pathname follow an accepted offset equal to the table length into a buffer that was fitted back down to strtab_size while strtab_term remained set, so strlen reads one byte past the allocation. No individual diff is a defect against the code it was written for: each one preserves the lookup, the terminator, or the fitted length that the other commits had not changed yet. Removing any one of those three commitments makes this input safe again, but each commitment is the maintenance that commit added (empty name at the end of a Windows table, a buffer the same length as the on-disk table, accepting that offset instead of reporting a missing name). A fix that keeps all three properties has to reconcile the fitted length with the spare-NUL contract rather than patching a single diff in isolation.
